Consumer refunds and warranties: a safe starting point

General information guide · Australia · reviewed 3 August 2026
Direct answer: A consumer dispute usually turns on what was promised, what was supplied, the condition of the goods or service, and which local consumer regime applies. Preserve the transaction record and use the current official complaint route before assuming a remedy.

Facts to establish first

Identify the country, state, province or region, the responsible body, the type of dispute or decision, and whether any formal notice or court paper has arrived. Do not submit names, identity numbers, addresses, case numbers or confidential documents here.

Evidence to preserve

  • Receipt, invoice or payment record
  • Product description, advertisement or written promise
  • Photos, inspection notes and a dated fault timeline
  • Messages showing when and how the issue was raised

A safer next-step sequence

  1. Build a one-page dated chronology from original records and separate facts from assumptions.
  2. Check the responsible body’s current process, forms, fees and deadlines; do not rely on an old article or a figure from another jurisdiction.
  3. If consequences are serious, formal papers have arrived or a deadline may be approaching, ask a qualified local lawyer to review the originals promptly.

Official routes to check

  • ACCC consumer information — Check the body’s current page before acting.
  • Attorney-General’s Department legal assistance — Check the body’s current page before acting.
  • Australian Government services — Check the body’s current page before acting.

Common questions

Can this guide decide my case?
No. It can organise a general issue and evidence, but applying law to a person’s full circumstances requires qualified local advice.
Why are there no fixed fees, limits or deadlines?
Those figures change and can differ by location and procedure. The responsible body’s current page or formal notice controls.
Should I send documents to the assistant?
No. Remove names, identity numbers, addresses, case numbers and all personal or confidential information. Describe only the general structure of the issue.

Ask AILawyer to organise a general question into facts, evidence and an official route. Do not send personal or confidential information.
